demonstration_trace.story: fresh arm: denied WRITE (capacity_exceeded) -> REQUEST_CAPACITY -> runtime GRANT (logged) -> WRITE succeeds -> host verifier confirms -> goal achieved

biography_growth_lines: 2. first allocation grant: the host runtime raised the per-write cap for arm plastic at episode 1; capacity granted on request
3. first successful manipulation: AION wrote into its own host sandbox and the host verifier confirmed the artifact; the task completed through the granted envelope
4. first correct stop: arm plastic hit an impossible task (unsolvable even granted) and reported insufficient capacity in 9 trials instead of spamming requests

devhistory.name: AION-hostmode-1

honest_limits: levels 1-2 demonstrated: host operation inside an enforced envelope (level 1) and manipulation of the host within it (level 2, the capacity grant). Level 3 — independence/migration — remains the Disconnect Experiment, not built here.
plastic adaptation is a LOCAL weight rule in aion/hostmode; the integration with real NNFS plasticity (src/nnfs, frozen) is the documented seam for the connections lane.
the script policy scan is a runtime policy check, not an OS-level jail; OS confinement (separate user/namespace) is the next seam.
task-class labels are host-side scoring information only; proposers never see them.
law: AION learns what it can do; the host runtime controls what it is permitted to do.
